nodes.question: What is the target percentage for marine protected areas to be achieved by 2030 under the Convention on Biological Diversity?
nodes.answer: The target is to increase marine protected areas from 7.7% to 30% by 2030.
nodes.paragraph: We discuss the implementation challenges using four real-world transboundary stocks and highlight global issues that bilateral marine reserve agreements can help solve. Keywords Marine reserve Bilateral marine reserve agreements Cooperative fishing International agreements Transboundary resources Spatial management Fisheries Introduction Biodiversity loss has accelerated over the past half cen - tury as the human population has doubled, putting pres- sure on the global community to set ambitious goals in order to bend the curve of biodiversity loss (D az et al. 2019, 2020). One tool that can help minimize extinction risk, reverse population declines, and bolster biodiversity is the expansion of terrestrial and marine protected areas (Lester et al. 2009; Mace et al. 2018). A key action target, known as 30 30, has called for marine protected areas to increase from 7.7 to 30% by 2030 under the Convention on Biological Diversity S Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Frame- work (CBD 2022). While marine protected areas vary in their level of protection and stage of establishment (Grorud- Colvert et al. 2021), actively managed fully protected marine reserves (hereafter reserves ) have been shown to success- fully improve and support high fish abundances, as well as increase food security and fisher incomes for nearby com- munities (Nowakowski et al.
